unmapped: Each examined item incurs a random cost Y_{i,t} in [0,1] with unknown mean c_i; net reward = cascade reward (1 if some examined item has state 1) minus total examination cost
Learner chooses an ordered list of any length and when to stop examining
Item states are Bernoulli(theta_i); costs bounded in [0,1]
Assumption 1: theta_i != c_i for all i and c_i > epsilon for a known constant epsilon > 0 (the learner knows epsilon, used by CC-UCB)
settings.definition_quote: Let $X_{i,t}$ be the state of arm $i\in[K]$ in step $t$. Then, $X_{i,t} \in \{0,1\}$ evolves according to an i.i.d. Bernoulli distribution with parameter $\theta_i$. Denote $Y_{i,t}$ as the cost of pulling arm $i$ in step $t$, where $Y_{i,t} \in [0,1]$ evolves according to an i.i.d. unknown distribution with $\Eb[Y_{i,t}] = c_i$. ... net reward ... $r_t := 1-\prod_{i=1}^{|\tilde{I}_t|} (1-X_{\tilde{I}_t(i),t})-\sum_{i=1}^{|\tilde{I}_t|} Y_{\tilde{I}_t(i),t}.$

symbols.D_i: c_i - theta_i (paper's Delta_i), cost mean minus state mean of item i

conditions: c_i > epsilon for all i (epsilon known)
sum is over items not in the optimal list I^* (items with theta_i/c_i < 1)
tuning: padding u_{i,t} = sqrt(alpha log t / N_{i,t})

source.label: thm:online
source.quote: Denote $\Delta_{i} := c_i - \theta_i$. The accumulative regret under Algorithm~\ref{alg:online2} is upper bounded as follows: \begin{align*} R(T)\leq \sum_{i \in [K]\backslash I^*} c_i\frac{16\alpha \log T}{\Delta^{2}_{i}} + O(1), \end{align*}

results.notes: Leading term is exact with an additive O(1) instance-dependent constant; recorded with notation O and '+1' standing for the O(1). Regret is measured against the optimal offline policy (UCR-T1), in expectation. sum_subopt is over [K]\I^*.

symbols.theta_i: Bernoulli state mean of item i

conditions: policy is alpha-consistent: sequentially pulls arms in I_t until a state 1 is observed and E[sum_t 1(I_t != I^*)] = o(T^alpha) for any alpha in (0,1)
sum over items not in I^*

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Under any $\alpha$-consistent policy, \begin{align*} \liminf_{T \rightarrow \infty} \frac{R(T)}{\log T} \geq \sum_{i \in [K]\backslash I^*}\frac{c_i - \theta_i}{d(\theta_i;c_i)}\quad \mbox{almost surely}, \end{align*} where $d(\theta_i; c_i)$ is the KL divergence of Bernoulli distributions with means $\theta_i$ and $c_i$.

results.notes: Paper says 'almost surely' but R(T) is an expectation; recorded as asymptotic. Proof borrows pull-count lower bound from Kveton et al. 2015.
